newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton unchanged despite foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton unchanged despite foreign buying.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates closed unchanged on Wednesday, despite small-scale buying by Japanese and Indonesian importers, brokers said.
A Japanese buyer purchased 1,000 375-lb bales at 69.20 U.S. cents per pound FOB on Monday and Indonesia 600 bales at 73.50 U.S. cents per pound C&F on Sunday, broker Nasim Usman said.

A member of the private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said cotton export registration, including those two deals, had reached 23,103 bales by Monday, compared to 2.084 million bales by the same date last year.
Usman attributed the sharp fall in exports to high domestic prices. "Exports could pick up if prices fall to 2,000 rupees per maund (37.32 kg)," he said.
Usman said prices were steady at the moment because spinners were well-stocked and were staying out of the market.

A member of the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association said ginneries had unsold stocks of 1.8 million bales. Cotton output in 1996/97 (July-June) had reached 8.335 million bales by Sunday, down from 9.481 million bales a year earlier.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 was quoted at 2,250 to 2,350 rupees per maund, Usman said.
